exploration.description: Browse all academic areas even if they did not appear in your matches. Pick an area to answer one optional refinement question or browse available programmes.

rules.core_checkpoint: Always available after 12 questions; display supported families or disciplines; no requirement to dive deeper.
rules.entry: User chooses Refine My Matches or Explore Something Different; any area may be explored even if absent from core results.
rules.routing: Select target area explicitly or use the strongest supported area; never auto-route to an unasked niche solely from the catalogue.
rules.unselected_options: No negative signal; skip/unsure gives no signal.
rules.answer_evidence: Deduplicate by question ID per discipline; two options selected in one question count as one independent supporting question.
rules.core_stability: Freeze core interest scores and initial recommendation order; optional replies create a labelled refined view and do not rewrite the initial results.
rules.within_family_scoring: For each candidate discipline, calculate direct support as count of distinct positively supporting questions (core + follow-up), and specificity as count of distinct question-level direct signals. Do not sum raw number of tags or catalogue entries. Compare only within the selected academic family. Normalise for each candidate by the number of applicable questions presented; never score unasked follow-ups as disagreements.
rules.eligibility: Specialised top-match promotion needs support from at least two distinct questions, including at least one directly relevant answer, and sufficient separation from sister disciplines. Thresholds for separation remain to be empirically calibrated; ties remain family-level.
rules.one_followup: If a candidate receives only one unique supporting question, surface it as a labelled exploration suggestion, not as a confirmed top match.
rules.cross_family: Refining family A cannot reduce the core score of family B. Explore Something Different may append a separately labelled exploration area but must not silently displace core top matches.
rules.explicit_negative: A genuine negative Likert response may count as counterevidence only for its stated interest; not selecting a scenario option never indicates dislike.
rules.explanations: Generate factual why-this-might-interest-you from at most 2-3 distinct positively answered question IDs plus a reviewed discipline description. Never claim aptitude or match probability; never infer specific interests without explicit evidence.
rules.unmapped_disciplines: Keep as browsable with insufficient questionnaire evidence; flag for mapping review; no auto-assignment based on NUS programme name.
rules.catalogue_independence: Adding/removing/renaming AU programmes cannot change any core or refined discipline score or evidence count.
rules.presentation: Top Qualities remain cautiously phrased as expressed preferences; Explore Similar Majors is navigable and compact.
rules.qs: QS is optional sorting/display later and never affects interest scoring.
